Key observation: For any pair, $\gcd(a_i, a_j) \cdot \text{lcm}(a_i, a_j) = a_i \cdot a_j$.

So from the 90 numbers, we can compute all products $a_i \cdot a_j$ for $i \neq j$. That gives us 45 products.

An alternative assignment: 
$$\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$$

$$\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$$

Another:
$$\begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$$

Gives $a_1 = q, a_2 = p, a_3 = pq$. Same set.

So in this case, all valid assignments give the same set. That's because the valuation vectors $(1,0), (0,1), (1,1)$ are "matched" — you can't reassign without creating duplicates or changing the set.
